items.labelEn: Ring-oscillator delay per stage, 28 nm FD-SOI, 296 K, 1.0 V
items.labelFr: Délai par étage d’un oscillateur en anneau, FD-SOI 28 nm, 296 K, 1,0 V
items.conditions: STMicroelectronics 28 nm UTBB FD-SOI (GO1, LVT, flip-well), 101-stage RO, T = 296 K, VDD = 1.0 V, no back bias (VN-WELL = VP-WELL = 0 V, uncompensated VTH).
items.protocol: Measured on wafer: 101-stage inverter ring oscillator (LVT flip-well, LG = 34 nm, WN = 420 nm, WP = 600 nm) with enabling AND gate and /1024 frequency divider; tP derived from RO frequency; protocol summarised in Table I of the paper.
items.locator: Table II (comparison of RO performance at 296 K and 4.3 K), row T = 296 K, VDD = 1 V
items.confidenceNotes: Quote is the flattened PDF text of Table II (columns VTH_NMOS, VN-WELL, T, VDD, tP, IDYN, ISTAT...); same row gives 27 ps at 0.8 V and 14 ps at 1.2 V. A ring-oscillator stage delay is close to, but not the same as, an FO4 delay (fan-out 1 here).

items.labelEn: Ring-oscillator delay per stage, 28 nm FD-SOI, 4.3 K, 0.325 V with forward body bias
items.labelFr: Délai par étage d’un oscillateur en anneau, FD-SOI 28 nm, 4,3 K, 0,325 V sous polarisation arrière directe
items.conditions: Same 101-stage RO, T = 4.3 K, VDD = 0.325 V, forward body bias VN-WELL = 4 V and VP-WELL = -5.8 V; static current 7 nA/stage.
items.protocol: Measured on wafer: 101-stage inverter ring oscillator (LVT flip-well, LG = 34 nm, WN = 420 nm, WP = 600 nm) with enabling AND gate and /1024 frequency divider; tP derived from RO frequency; protocol summarised in Table I of the paper. Cryogenic measurement between 296 K and 4.3 K.
items.locator: Abstract; Sec. III and Table III (row VDD = 0.325 V)
items.quote: excellent RO performance with tP=37ps and ISTAT=7nA/stage are demonstrated at VDD = 0.325V
items.confidenceNotes: Operating point chosen for energy efficiency, not maximum speed; shows that cryogenic operation at very low VDD keeps tens-of-ps delays.

items.labelEn: Oscillation frequency of the 101-stage ring oscillator, 28 nm FD-SOI, 296 K, 1.0 V
items.labelFr: Fréquence d’oscillation de l’anneau à 101 étages, FD-SOI 28 nm, 296 K, 1,0 V
items.conditions: Derived from tP = 18 ps and N = 101 stages (before the /1024 divider); f = 1/(2·N·tP).
items.locator: Sec. II (101 identical stages) and Table II
items.quote: The RO consists of 101 identical stages together with an enabling two-way AND gate.
items.confidenceNotes: The paper reports tP, not f; f is back-computed with the usual RO relation, which the paper uses implicitly (tP derived from f). Rounded.

items.labelEn: SiGe HBT transit frequency fT, IHP SG13G2 (0.13 µm BiCMOS)
items.labelFr: Fréquence de transition fT du TBH SiGe, IHP SG13G2 (BiCMOS 0,13 µm)
items.conditions: IHP SG13G2 0.13 µm SiGe:C BiCMOS, npn HBT, peak value; bias and device geometry not stated on the page; process of the open-source PDK.
items.quote: SG13G2 has the same device portfolio as SG13S but much higher bipolar performance with f T = 300 GHz and 500 GHz maximum oscillation frequency.
items.confidenceNotes: Foundry peak figure; circuits run far below fT. Same figures in the Europractice brochure.

items.labelEn: SiGe HBT maximum oscillation frequency fmax, IHP SG13G2
items.labelFr: Fréquence maximale d’oscillation fmax du TBH SiGe, IHP SG13G2
items.conditions: IHP SG13G2 0.13 µm SiGe:C BiCMOS, npn HBT, peak value.
items.quote: f T = 300 GHz and 500 GHz maximum oscillation frequency
items.confidenceNotes: Foundry peak figure.

items.labelEn: SiGe HBT transit frequency fT, IHP SG13G3
items.labelFr: Fréquence de transition fT du TBH SiGe, IHP SG13G3
items.conditions: IHP SG13G3 0.13 µm SiGe:C BiCMOS, 7-layer Al BEOL (Cu variant SG13G3Cu), research/prototyping only; "up to" value.
items.quote: fT= 470 GHz, fmax = 650 GHz
items.confidenceNotes: MPW broker brochure relaying IHP figures; offered only for research and prototyping.

items.labelEn: SiGe HBT maximum oscillation frequency fmax, IHP SG13G3
items.labelFr: Fréquence maximale d’oscillation fmax du TBH SiGe, IHP SG13G3
items.conditions: IHP SG13G3 / SG13G3Cu, "up to" value.
items.locator: p. 1, SG13G3Cu description paragraph; p. 2 technology table
items.quote: up to 650 GHz maximum oscillation
items.confidenceNotes: Same caveats as fT.

items.labelEn: Maximum oscillation frequency fmax of a 25 nm InP HEMT (Northrop Grumman, 2015)
items.labelFr: Fréquence maximale d’oscillation fmax d’un HEMT InP à grille de 25 nm (Northrop Grumman, 2015)
items.conditions: Northrop Grumman InP HEMT, recessed T-gate Ti/Pt/Au with 25 nm footprint; extrapolated value; associated amplifier: 9 dB gain at 1.0 THz.
items.protocol: On-wafer S-parameter measurements of 25 nm-gate InP HEMTs; fT and fMAX obtained by extrapolating the measured gain to unity (as reported by the news item).
items.locator: News item, paragraph on device characterisation
items.quote: Extrapolating the data to unity gain gave a maximum oscillation frequency (fMAX) of 1.5THz.
items.confidenceNotes: Secondary source (trade press) for X. B. Mei et al., IEEE EDL 2015 (paywalled, not read). Extrapolated, not directly observed. Some secondary sources give a 32 nm node for the same work.

items.labelEn: Cut-off frequency fT of a 25 nm InP HEMT (Northrop Grumman, 2015)
items.labelFr: Fréquence de coupure fT d’un HEMT InP à grille de 25 nm (Northrop Grumman, 2015)
items.conditions: Same device as the fmax value.
items.protocol: On-wafer S-parameter measurements of 25 nm-gate InP HEMTs; fT and fMAX obtained by extrapolating the measured gain to unity (as reported by the news item).
items.locator: News item, paragraph on device characterisation
items.quote: The cut-off frequency (fT) was 650GHz.
items.confidenceNotes: Secondary source; a table in the same item reportedly gives 0.61 THz, so fT is uncertain at about ±7 %.

items.labelEn: Surface-code error-correction cycle time, Google Willow (105 qubits)
items.labelFr: Durée d’un cycle de correction d’erreurs (code de surface), Google Willow (105 qubits)
items.conditions: Google 105-qubit superconducting processor (Willow), surface-code memory up to distance 7 (101 qubits), 2024 experiment.
items.locator: Abstract; Sec. I and Sec. V (Real-time decoding)
items.quote: with a cycle time of 1.1 μs
items.confidenceNotes: Operating parameter of the experiment. One cycle at 4 GHz ≈ 4,400 CPU cycles.

items.labelEn: Mean qubit energy-relaxation time T1, Google Willow
items.labelFr: Temps de relaxation T1 moyen des qubits, Google Willow
items.conditions: 105-qubit Willow processor, mean over operating qubits at their operating points.
items.protocol: Mean of per-qubit T1 measured at the operating frequency on the 105-qubit processor (standard transmon characterisation, details in the paper's Supplementary Information); n = qubits of the device; spread not quoted here.
items.locator: Sec. II "A surface code memory below threshold", first paragraph
items.quote: The qubits have a mean operating T1 of 68 µs and T2,CPMG of 89 µs
items.confidenceNotes: Mean only; the distribution is in the paper's figures. Not a guaranteed device spec.

items.labelEn: Mean qubit coherence time T2 (CPMG), Google Willow
items.labelFr: Temps de cohérence T2 (CPMG) moyen des qubits, Google Willow
items.conditions: 105-qubit Willow processor, CPMG dynamical-decoupling sequence, mean over qubits.
items.protocol: Mean of per-qubit T2 measured with a CPMG sequence on the 105-qubit processor; details in the Supplementary Information.
items.locator: Sec. II "A surface code memory below threshold", first paragraph
items.quote: The qubits have a mean operating T1 of 68 µs and T2,CPMG of 89 µs
items.confidenceNotes: T2,CPMG is longer than a plain Ramsey T2*; do not compare directly with T2 values measured otherwise.

items.labelEn: Two-qubit CZ gate duration, Google Willow
items.labelFr: Durée d’une porte CZ à deux qubits, Google Willow
items.conditions: CZ gate on the 105-qubit processor (37 ns on the 72-qubit processor of the same study).
items.locator: Supplementary Information, Sec. I "Gates and Readout"
items.quote: Our CZ gates are performed in 42 ns on the 105-qubit processor, and 37 ns on the 72-qubit processor.
items.confidenceNotes: Pulse duration set by the experimenters, not an error-rate figure.

items.labelEn: Single-qubit XY rotation duration, Google Willow
items.labelFr: Durée d’une rotation XY à un qubit, Google Willow
items.conditions: All XY rotations on the 105-qubit processor.
items.locator: Supplementary Information, Sec. I "Gates and Readout"
items.quote: On the 105-qubit processor, all XY rotations have 25 ns duration
items.confidenceNotes: The same section gives 35 ns (π) and 18 ns (π/2) for another configuration; the 25 ns value is the one stated for the 105-qubit processor.

items.labelEn: Average real-time decoder latency, distance-5 surface code, Google Willow
items.labelFr: Latence moyenne du décodeur temps réel, code de surface de distance 5, Google Willow
items.conditions: 72-qubit processor experiment, distance-5 code, real-time decoding up to one million cycles at 1.1 µs per cycle.
items.protocol: Real-time decoding experiment: distance-5 surface code run for up to 10^6 cycles, decoder latency averaged over the run (paper Sec. V).
items.quote: achieving an average decoder latency of 63 μs at distance-5 up to a million cycles
items.confidenceNotes: Average only; decoder latency definition (time from end of final cycle to decoder output) is in Sec. V.

items.labelEn: Median qubit T1, IBM Heron R1 (ibm_montecarlo, 57-qubit subset)
items.labelFr: T1 médian des qubits, IBM Heron R1 (ibm_montecarlo, sous-ensemble de 57 qubits)
items.conditions: IBM Heron R1, 133-qubit ibm_montecarlo, fixed-frequency transmons with tunable couplers; median over 57 selected qubits; device properties of 16 June 2024 (whole-device median also 1.8 × 10^2 µs).
items.protocol: IBM backend calibration data for Heron R1 ibm_montecarlo on 16 June 2024 (T1 from standard relaxation experiments, gate errors from randomized benchmarking); medians over the 57-qubit subset selected for the k = 1 experiment.
items.locator: Sec. III "Device details", paragraph after Fig. 10 (k = 1 subset)
items.quote: median properties: T1 = 180µs, T2 = 150µs
items.confidenceNotes: Calibration snapshot: IBM values drift daily; other Heron papers report 145-187 µs. Subset chosen among best qubits, so slightly optimistic.

items.labelEn: Two-qubit gate length, IBM Heron R1 (ibm_montecarlo)
items.labelFr: Durée de la porte à deux qubits, IBM Heron R1 (ibm_montecarlo)
items.conditions: Heron R1 ibm_montecarlo, native CZ, median over the 57-qubit subset, 16 June 2024; 88 ns median on the k = 3 subset.
items.quote: two-qubit gate error 0.24% and length 104ns
items.confidenceNotes: Calibrated pulse length reported by the backend; varies by subset (88-104 ns) and date; other papers give 68-80 ns for ibm_torino/ibm_fez.

items.labelEn: Single-qubit gate length, IBM Heron R1 (ibm_montecarlo)
items.labelFr: Durée d’une porte à un qubit, IBM Heron R1 (ibm_montecarlo)
items.conditions: Heron R1 ibm_montecarlo, median over the 57-qubit subset, 16 June 2024; readout length 2 µs on the same subset.
items.quote: single-qubit gate error 0.022% and length 32ns
items.confidenceNotes: Backend-reported pulse length.

items.labelEn: Spin-orbit-torque MRAM switching time, imec 62 nm device
items.labelFr: Durée de commutation d’une MRAM à couple spin-orbite, dispositif imec de 62 nm
items.conditions: imec 300 mm SOT-MRAM, 62 nm MTJ, W-based SOT underlayer, ~1 V critical voltage at 50 % switching probability, in-plane field < 23 mT; research device, 2018.
items.protocol: Electrical switching of the same 62 nm top-pinned perpendicular MTJ on a W-based SOT track (300 mm imec integration): switching probability vs. pulse voltage and length, critical voltage at 50 % probability (Fig. 6); SOT with < 23 mT in-plane field, STT at zero field.
items.quote: SOT demonstrates reliable switching down to 210 ps with
items.confidenceNotes: Shortest write pulse on a research cell, not a product write latency (no peripheral circuitry). Needs an assisting field.

items.labelEn: Shortest STT write pulse on the same imec MTJ
items.labelFr: Impulsion d’écriture STT la plus courte sur la même jonction imec
items.conditions: Same 62 nm device switched by spin-transfer torque at zero field; pulse length limited to avoid barrier breakdown; ~470 fJ.
items.protocol: Electrical switching of the same 62 nm top-pinned perpendicular MTJ on a W-based SOT track (300 mm imec integration): switching probability vs. pulse voltage and length, critical voltage at 50 % probability (Fig. 6); SOT with < 23 mT in-plane field, STT at zero field.
items.quote: In STT case, τp is limited to 5ns to avoid breakdown
items.confidenceNotes: Limit for this device, not a general STT-MRAM bound; contrast with 210 ps for SOT.

items.labelEn: GPS satellite orbit altitude (MEO)

items.labelFr: Temps de trajet d’un signal depuis un satellite GPS au zénith

items.quote: at an altitude of 35 786 km

items.labelFr: Débit de l’Ethernet 400 gigabits

items.confidenceNotes: Same method as the existing 1G/10G/100G corpus items; at 400 Gbit/s the result is 1.68 ns.

items.labelEn: White Rabbit (PTP extension) time synchronisation accuracy
items.labelFr: Précision de synchronisation temporelle de White Rabbit (extension de PTP)
items.conditions: Upper bound: "sub-nanosecond accuracy" with picosecond precision, thousands of nodes, typical 10 km links; extension of PTP incorporated in IEEE 1588-2019 (High Accuracy profile).
items.quote: sub-nanosecond accuracy and picoseconds precision of synchronization
items.confidenceNotes: Bound, not a measured statistic; plain PTP on ordinary networks is far less accurate.

items.labelEn: Typical NTP accuracy on a LAN
items.labelFr: Précision typique de NTP sur un réseau local

items.quote: It provides accuracies typically less than a millisecond on LANs and up to a few milliseconds on WANs.
items.confidenceNotes: Order of magnitude given by the maintainers, no measurement protocol.

items.quote: capable of supporting a maximum throughput of at least 30 Gbps
items.confidenceNotes: Lower bound of a design target; the Wi-Fi Alliance page gives no number.

items.labelFr: Intervalle de connexion minimal du Bluetooth LE (avant Core 6.2)

items.labelEn: Bluetooth LE maximum connection interval
items.labelFr: Intervalle de connexion maximal du Bluetooth LE

items.labelEn: Starlink median peak-hour latency, United States (June 2025)
items.labelFr: Latence médiane de Starlink aux heures de pointe, États-Unis (juin 2025)
items.conditions: All US customers, peak hours, as of June 2025; latency = router-to-internet round trip; fewer than 1 % of US measurements exceed 55 ms.
items.protocol: Operator telemetry: anonymised latency measurements collected from millions of Starlink routers every 15 seconds (router to internet and back); median over US customers at peak hours.
items.quote: As of June 2025, Starlink is delivering median peak-hour latency of 25.7 milliseconds (ms) across all customers in the United States
items.confidenceNotes: Vendor self-report; exact endpoint of "the internet" and peak-hour definition not given; no independent audit.

items.labelEn: Starlink satellite-hop latency, U.S. Virgin Islands (July 2025, mean)
items.labelFr: Latence du saut satellite Starlink, îles Vierges américaines (juillet 2025, moyenne)
items.conditions: Mean RTT difference between user router and its home PoP (mmmiflx1), U.S. Virgin Islands, July 2025 (54 ms in May 2025).
items.protocol: TTL-limited ICMP probing from a cloud vantage point (Singapore, Alibaba Cloud): two echo requests per target with different TTLs to reach the user router and its home PoP; 100 randomly sampled router IPv6 addresses per region, one probe every 3 s, one-hour window per region; mean of the latency difference.
items.quote: U.S. Virgin Islands 54 43
items.confidenceNotes: Mean, not median; estimate of the satellite segment only (excludes PoP-to-server path). Quote is the flattened HTML text of the Table III row.
